category.title: Arms
category.intro: Equipment-free programmes for the back of the upper arm (triceps) and the front (biceps). You work the triceps with push-up and dip variations, and the biceps with your own resistance, a door frame and rows under a table.
science: The diamond push-up is one of the moves that works the triceps most; chair dips are a good start.
The lowering part, where the muscle resists while lengthening, is the most important part for gains; that's why you lower slowly in the biceps moves.
Working "against your own resistance", using one hand to load the other arm, increased strength and arm size in a small study.
Evidence for equipment-free biceps training is limited; the programme tries to balance this with holds in a lengthened position and slow lowering.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.setup: Stand tall and open your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
steps: Draw small circles with your arms.
Slowly make the circles bigger.
Change direction halfway through.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
exercises.mistake: Don't swing them fast and jerkily.

exercises.name: Wall Triceps Press
exercises.setup: Stand a step away from a wall, lean forward and rest your forearms on the wall; hands at eye level.
steps: Push with your palms to straighten your elbows; your elbows come off the wall.
Pause briefly when your arms are straight.
Slowly lower your forearms back to the wall.
exercises.tip: The further your feet are from the wall, the harder the move.
exercises.mistake: Don't stick your hips out; keep your body straight.

exercises.name: Kneeling Diamond Push-Up
exercises.setup: Knees on the floor. Bring your hands together under your chest; thumbs and index fingers form a diamond.
steps: Keeping your elbows close to your body, lower your chest towards your hands.
Stop when your chest nears your hands.
Push back up to straighten your arms.
exercises.tip: The easier version of the diamond push-up; lift your knees after 15 clean reps.
exercises.mistake: Don't flare your elbows out; let them bend backwards.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.setup: Push-up position; bring your hands together under your chest with your fingers forming a diamond.
steps: Keeping your elbows close to your body, lower your chest towards your hands.
Stop when your chest nears your hands.
Push back up.
exercises.tip: If your wrists strain, spread your hands a little.

exercises.name: Chair Dips
exercises.setup: Stand in front of a sturdy chair placed against a wall. Put your hands behind you on the edge of the chair, knees bent.
steps: Bend your elbows backwards and lower your hips.
Stop when your elbows reach 90 degrees.
Push up with your palms.
exercises.tip: Keep your hips close to the chair.
exercises.mistake: Don't hunch your shoulders towards your ears; if your shoulder hurts, go down less.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Dips
exercises.setup: Chair dip position, but with your legs straight and heels on the floor.
steps: Bend your elbows backwards and lower your hips.
Stop when your elbows reach 90 degrees.
Push back up.
exercises.tip: The further away your legs are, the more of your body your arms carry.
exercises.mistake: Don't rush the lowering; go down slowly.

exercises.name: Plank Up-Down
exercises.setup: Start in a forearm plank: forearms on the floor, body straight.
steps: Place one hand, then the other, on the floor to straighten your arms; come up into a push-up position.
Lower one elbow, then the other, back to the forearm plank.
Switch the leading arm every round.
exercises.tip: Spreading your feet a little makes your hips sway less.
exercises.mistake: Don't sway your hips sideways or lift them up.

exercises.name: Self-Resistance Biceps Curl
exercises.setup: Stand up. Keep the elbow of the working arm close to your waist, palm facing up. Put your other hand on the wrist of the working arm.
steps: Curl the working arm up while pressing down with your other hand.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly over 3 seconds, resisting with your other hand; switch arms halfway through.
exercises.tip: Give as much resistance as lets you move slowly but without stopping; the real work is on the way down.
exercises.mistake: Don't lift your elbow forward; keep it at your waist.

exercises.name: Door Frame Biceps Hold
exercises.setup: Hold the sturdy frame of an open door with both hands at chest height, palms facing up. Bring your feet close to the frame and lean back.
steps: Lean back, keeping your elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Tense as if pulling yourself towards the frame with your arms.
Keep breathing and hold.
exercises.tip: The closer your feet are to the frame, the harder the move.
exercises.mistake: Don't do it if the frame isn't sturdy; if your hands slip, let go and stand up.

exercises.name: Under-Table Row (Palms Up)
exercises.setup: Lie on your back under a sturdy table. Hold the edge of the table shoulder-width apart with your palms facing you.
steps: Bend your elbows and pull your chest towards the table.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.tip: With palms facing up the biceps work more; bending your knees makes it easier.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your hips drop; make sure the table won't tip over.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.setup: From a push-up position, lift your hips up; your body forms an upside-down V.
steps: Bend your elbows to bring your head towards the floor.
Stop when your head nears the floor.
Push back up to straighten your arms.
exercises.tip: Bending your elbows backwards works the triceps more.
exercises.mistake: Don't bump your head on the floor; keep the lowering slow.

exercises.name: Push-Up Hold
exercises.setup: Get into a push-up position and lower halfway; elbows at about 90 degrees.
steps: Stay at this height.
Body straight, belly tight.
Keep breathing and hold until the time is up.
exercises.tip: If it's too hard, hold with your knees on the floor.
